newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures drift to end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures drift to end narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures drifted inside of Monday's ranges to end narrowly mixed.
Traders said profit-takers finally emerged following the last two trading sessions which powered September T-bonds to a seven-month high at 113-31/32 on Monday.
The market had little reaction to any of the minor U.S. economic reports that were released on Tuesday, including the U.S. retail sales index by Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook.
The index rose 1.7 percent, as expected, and followed a 0.1-percent rise in U.S. BTM/Schroders' weekly U.S. chain store sales data on Tuesday morning.
U.S. May consumer credit rose $3.0 billion in May versus forecasts for a $5.6 billion rise and against April's revised rise of $9.7 billion rise.
September T-bonds mustered a brief rise to 113-28/32 on light local short-covering, but for most of the day traded below minor resistance at 113-25/32.
Traders expect the market to back-and-fill within ranges given the lack of fresh news, anticipation ahead of Friday's U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) and slightly overbought conditions.

Some also said decent corporate offerings, with high-profile companies expected to launch sizable deals, dragged down the market. Dealers said issuers were tempted to sell long-duration bonds in order to capitalize on bullish investor sentiment.

At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds were down 01/32 at 113-20/32, 10-year notes were unchanged at 109-12/32, December T-bills were off 0.005 at 94.745, munibonds were up 01/32 at 119-01/32 and December Eurodollars were flat at 94.01. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
